title: Derivative of Reciprocal Square Root from First Principles
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find f'(x) for f(x) = 1/sqrt(x) for x > 0 using the definition of derivative.

steps.title: Formulate the Difference Quotient
steps.explanation: Combine the fractions in the numerator with common denominator sqrt(x)*sqrt(x+h).

steps.title: Rationalize Using the Conjugate
steps.mathExpression: \frac{(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x + h})(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + h})}{h\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x + h}(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + h})} = \frac{x - (x + h)}{h\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x + h}(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + h})} = \frac{-h}{h\dots} = \frac{-1}{\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x + h}(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + h})}
steps.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt(x) + sqrt(x+h) and cancel h.
steps.why: Conjugate multiplication rationalizes the radical numerator.

steps.title: Evaluate Limit as h -> 0
steps.explanation: Substitute h = 0 into the continuous simplified expression.
steps.why: Taking the limit produces the power rule derivative for n = -1/2.
